title: feat(spec): the dataset tools' output declares nextStep on list_datasets and sourceLine on query_dataset (ADR-0149 M1)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBLW6dHPW6sSheA32XPKZzPV)_

Fixes #34918

Clause-②: yes (widening: two optional output members on published schemas)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md (follows `nextStep` and cites `sourceLine` once the executor fills them)

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:两个问数工具的返回结构各加一个可选成员。`list_datasets` 加 `nextStep`:平台按 D3 选数规则读用户的词,读到的是四种情况里的哪一种(命中一个度量、命中多个度量、只有候选、没有度量),说的是哪些词,外加一句成文的话。`query_dataset` 加 `sourceLine`:答案出处的一句成文的话。ADR-0149 M1 末尾加一段只增不改的修订说明。本 PR 只声明形状,不改执行器。
- 为什么改:#34894 的裁决(选 A,记录 6953671481,原话「两件都同意：构建提交进仓库，#34894 选 A」):下一步和出处这两句话由平台执行器写进工具返回,产品自己的 AI 和 MCP 客户端读到的是同一份;规范只声明形状,句子的文字不进规范,M1 不变。
- 风险与回滚:只加两个可选输出成员,不带它们的返回解析结果与之前相同。执行器在 #34919 填充,它落地前没有返回会带这两个成员,但 MCP 客户端读到的 `outputSchema` 从本 PR 起就多出这两项。`decision` 的四个取值发布后即对外契约,之后改名是破坏性变更。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:① `packages/spec/src/ai/dataset-tools.zod.ts` 里 `DatasetNextStepDecision` 的四个取值和 `decision` 的 `.describe()` 文字:取值写的是「平台查到了什么」,不是「接下来该怎么做」;② 同一文件里 `nextStep.terms`:它按词指向同一份返回里的 `matches` 与 `candidates`,自己不再列成员,理由在下面 Schema decisions;③ `docs/adr/0149-ai-answers-business-questions-through-the-dataset-semantic-layer.md` M1 末尾的修订说明,看它是否如实转述裁决。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/ai/dataset-tools.test.ts`,预期 `Tests  44 passed (44)`。
- 需要你做的:席位 L2 复核后,亲手合并本 PR(Tier H:`docs/adr/**` 与 `packages/spec/**`)。

## What changes

- **`packages/spec/src/ai/dataset-tools.zod.ts`** (100 lines added, 2 removed; the two removed lines are module doc block lines, rewritten to name the two members):
  - `ListDatasetsOutputSchema` gains one optional member, `nextStep`, a `DatasetNextStepSchema`.
  - `DatasetNextStepSchema` (type `DatasetNextStep`): `{ decision, terms, note }`, all three required. `decision` is `DatasetNextStepDecision`; `terms` is a list of strings with at least one entry; `note` is a non-empty string.
  - `DatasetNextStepDecision`: a closed enum, `one_measure`, `several_measures`, `candidates_only`, `no_measure`.
  - `QueryDatasetOutputSchema` gains one optional member, `sourceLine`, a non-empty string, declared in the tool's own `.extend()` beside `provenance`.
  - `candidates`, `matches`, `provenance`, `AnalyticsResultResponseSchema` and every other declaration are untouched.
- **`packages/spec/src/ai/dataset-tools.test.ts`**: eleven new cases (44 run in the file now). Seven in a new `list_datasets nextStep` block, two in the `query_dataset output` block, two in the JSON Schema projection block.
- **`packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`**: two pin rows for the two new aliases and the pinned count 858 to 860. `check:spec-parsed-alias` (ADR-0122) refuses a new bare input alias with no pin.
- **Generated, by the generators only** (`check:generated --fix`): `packages/spec/{api-surface,authorable-surface,declaration-map,export-origins,json-schema.manifest}/ai.json`, `content/docs/references/ai/dataset-tools.mdx`, `content/docs/references/index.mdx` (schema total 1670 to 1672, AI 82 to 84), `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/ai.md` (97 to 98 object sites). `authorable-surface.base.json` did not move.
- **`docs/adr/0149-ai-answers-business-questions-through-the-dataset-semantic-layer.md`**: an amendment note at the end of M1, in the form of the note under D3. 11 lines added, 0 removed or changed.
- **`.changeset/34918-dataset-next-step-source-line.md`**: `@objectstack/spec` at `minor`.
- Nothing under `packages/services/**`, `packages/mcp/**` or `skills/**`.

## Why

Ruled by the maintainer on #34894, option A, verbatim 「两件都同意：构建提交进仓库，#34894 选 A」 (ruling record `6953671481`). The record states what was ruled: the framework's executor returns `nextStep` (a closed decision, the candidates, a sentence) on `list_datasets` and `sourceLine` on `query_dataset`; the spec declares the shapes; the sentence's text is the executor's and does not enter the spec, so ADR-0149 M1 (ruled A) stands.

Today a client that asks through MCP is handed `matches` and `candidates` and works out what they mean, and what to cite, by itself. With the two members every client that made the call reads the same conclusion and the same source line from the result.

This PR is the spec half: the shapes, and the record. The executor that fills both members is #34919.

## Schema decisions

| Point | Card or ruling | Settled here | Why |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `decision` values | a closed enum covering one metric matches, several match, near candidates only, nothing | `one_measure`, `several_measures`, `candidates_only`, `no_measure` | Lowercase `snake_case`, the casing AGENTS.md gives data values (Prime Directive 3). The cases are counted in measures because D3 selects a measure. The set is the four cases the card names and no more. |
| What a value names | not stated | what the platform found, not what a reader then does | M1 A keeps guidance out of the spec, so no value is an instruction (`ask`, `use`, `fallback`). What follows from each case is D3's to say. M2 (the fallback posture) names its own revisits: a re-ruling of what to do in a case leaves the four findings as they are. |
| A term that equals only a dimension | not stated | `no_measure`; no fifth value | D3 rule 5: a dimension alone is not an answer. The term keeps its entry in the dataset's `matches`, and the `decision` description says a dimension is not counted. |
| The reference to the candidates | "the candidates it rests on", without declaring #34761's list twice | `terms`: the caller's terms the decision is about. `nextStep` holds no member list | **Differs in form from the ruling record's "the candidates".** Every entry of `matches` and of `candidates` already carries the caller's `term`, so the terms are the join key: the members are read under them from the same answer. No `{ dataset, member }` pointer is declared a second time, so there is no second list that could disagree with the first. |
| `note` | a string slot whose text is the executor's | required inside `nextStep`, non-empty | A `nextStep` without its sentence would not be the ruled result. The spec fixes no wording, no template and no language. |
| One `nextStep` or one per term | "a closed decision" | one object per answer | When the caller's terms are in different cases, which case the answer reports is the executor's rule (#34919). `terms` says which terms the reported case is about. Raised in the dev report as an open question for #34919. |
| Presence of `nextStep` | optional | `.optional()`; described as present only when `terms` were sent | An answer without the key parses to the same value as before. A schema cannot tie an output member to the input; holding it is the executor's. |
| `sourceLine` | optional string | `z.string().min(1).optional()` | "No source line" has one spelling, the key's absence. An empty string does not parse. |
| Where `sourceLine` is declared | on the `query_dataset` output, without widening the shared response | in `QueryDatasetOutputSchema`'s own `.extend()`, beside `provenance` | The schema is already `AnalyticsResultResponseSchema.shape.data` with `sql` omitted and the tool's members added. Adding one more there leaves `AnalyticsResultResponseSchema` unedited; a test pins that the REST door's `data` shape has no `sourceLine`. |
| Description text | says what the member is for; no guidance | facts only | Each description says what the member is, who composes it and what it is composed from. None says what a model should do with it. |

The two new type aliases are bare input aliases with pins, not aliases paired with a `Parsed` twin: neither schema has a default or a transform, so input and output types are the same (ADR-0122).

## Known overlaps

`node scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs` exits 1 against two open PRs. The dispatching seat (area o3-E) read both overlaps and ordered the push.

| Open PR (head) | File | Where the two sides meet |
|:--|:--|:--|
| #34925 (`8f6048c352`), #34719 (`5a05e4f2f4`) | `packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts` | the pinned isomorphic-alias count (858 to 860 here): the header line, the case title, and the history comment with `toHaveLength`. The pin rows themselves merge |
| #34925 (`8f6048c352`), #34719 (`5a05e4f2f4`) | `content/docs/references/index.mdx` (generated) | the generated totals. The frontmatter description count and the Total row conflict (1672 here, 1671 there), in one hunk with the UI row (177 to 178 there). The AI row (82 to 84 here) moves beside them and merges |

Remedy for whichever lands second: merge `main`, re-run `gen:docs`, re-sum the pin count. No other file conflicts (`git merge-tree` against each fetched head, read hunk by hunk). #34928 (`3d92094558`) shares the ADR-0149 file, with a note under D3, and merges cleanly. This PR touches none of those PRs nor their branches.

## Outside the claimed surface

None. All 13 changed paths are in the claim's File surface (claim comment `6959561891`), the pin test and the two generated totals files included.

## Prior rulings read

The claim names these. None is crossed.

- **#34894 A** (`6953671481`): built as ruled. "The candidates" is carried by reference (card scope: one shape with #34761's `candidates`, not the same list twice).
- **ADR-0149 M1 A** (guidance text out of the spec): no sentence of guidance is added. The note under M1 changes no word of M1.
- **ADR-0149 D2** (two tools, one definition, one executor, two transports): each tool's one definition gains one optional member. No second definition, no executor and no transport changes.
- **ADR-0149 D3 and its amendment note**: what counts as a hit, the five rules and the candidates rule are untouched. `nextStep.decision` names which of those cases an answer is in.
- **#34691 F1 B** (the server returns candidates at zero match): `candidates` is unchanged and stays the one list.
- **ADR-0149 D6** (every key names its reader in its first implementation card): the note's "State on `main`" bullet names #34919 as the card that fills both members.

## Tests

Readings are on head `d10ea09296` with a clean working tree.

| Command | Result |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/ai/dataset-tools.test.ts src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts` (verify lock) | `Test Files  2 passed (2)`, `Tests  47 passed (47)`; lock line `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` (verify lock) | `check:test-typecheck: OK`; `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` (verify lock) | `Test Files  849 passed (849)`; `Tests  27213 passed \| 1 todo (27214)`; `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-analytics test` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp test` (verify lock) | service-analytics `Test Files  218 passed (218)`, `Tests  5560 passed \| 335 skipped (5895)`; mcp `Test Files  71 passed (71)`, `Tests  1252 passed (1252)`; `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` on the three changed TypeScript files | exit 0, no finding |

The two downstream packages are the ones outside spec that import the dataset-tool schemas (direction: consumers of spec). They ran against a spec `dist/` that carries the new members: the built `getDatasetToolJsonSchemas()` answers `nextStep` as `type: object`, `required: ["decision","terms","note"]`, `additionalProperties: false`, with the four-value enum, and `sourceLine` as `type: string`, `minLength: 1`, neither in its output's `required` list.

<details><summary>What the new cases pin</summary>

- `decision` takes each of the four values and refuses any other, at path `nextStep.decision`: an action word (`ask`), a near spelling (`one_match`), another casing (`ONE_MEASURE`), the empty string, a number and `null`.
- An answer with `nextStep` beside `candidates` parses and keeps both. An answer without the key parses to the same value as before.
- `decision`, `terms` and `note` are each required. An empty `terms` list and an empty `note` are refused.
- `nextStep` has exactly those three keys. A `{ dataset, member }` pointer in `terms` is refused at `terms.0`.
- One list of candidates: `ListDatasetsOutputSchema`'s `candidates` element is `DatasetTermCandidateSchema` itself, and a `candidates` or `matches` list written inside `nextStep` is not part of the shape (the parsed value does not carry it).
- The reference is by term: the members a decision rests on are found by filtering the same answer's `matches` and `candidates` on `nextStep.terms`.
- `sourceLine` is optional and non-empty; an empty string, a number, `null` and a list are refused at path `sourceLine`. An answer without it parses to the same value as before.
- `AnalyticsResultResponseSchema`'s `data` shape has no `sourceLine`, and a `sourceLine` sent to the door's `data` is not kept by its parse.
- The projected `list_datasets` `outputSchema`: `nextStep` is not in `required`; it is an object requiring `decision`, `note` and `terms`, with `additionalProperties: false`; `decision` is an enum of the four values; `terms` is an array of strings with `minItems` 1; `note` has `minLength` 1.
- The projected `query_dataset` `outputSchema`: `sourceLine` is a string with `minLength` 1 and is not in `required`.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (three, each restored)</summary>

Each mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on `dataset-tools.zod.ts`; each anchor hit exactly once and the blob changed; each restore ended with "ok restored: blob == HEAD (332deaf8eec5) and `git diff HEAD` is empty". The command under each mutation was the two-minute one above, under the verify lock. The suite imports the schema by relative path from `src/`, so there is no `dist/` leg.

| Mutation | Reading |
|:--|:--|
| a fifth value, `ask`, added to `DatasetNextStepDecision` (the enum no longer closed on the four) | `Tests  2 failed \| 42 passed (44)`: the four-cases case and the `list_datasets` projection case |
| `.optional()` dropped from `nextStep` | `Tests  6 failed \| 38 passed (44)`: the `nextStep` "without the key" case, the `nextStep` projection case, and four earlier cases (three whose answers carry no `nextStep`, one that reads the output's `required` list) |
| `.optional()` dropped from `sourceLine` | `Tests  4 failed \| 40 passed (44)`: the `sourceLine` case, its projection case, and two earlier `query_dataset` cases whose answers carry no `sourceLine` |

After the last restore the two files ran green again: `Test Files  2 passed (2)`, `Tests  47 passed (47)`.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **The members are declared and nothing fills them yet.** Until #34919 lands no answer carries `nextStep` or `sourceLine`. Each tool's `outputSchema` lists its optional member from this PR on. The ADR note says so in its last bullet.
- **What the schema cannot refuse is the executor's to hold** (#34919): that `decision` is the case the named terms are in, that every term in `nextStep.terms` was sent, and that `nextStep` is present only when `terms` were sent. The TSDoc on `DatasetNextStepSchema` says so.
- **Terms in different cases.** One answer reports one case. Which case wins when the caller's terms are in several is not ruled and not in the spec; it is raised for #34919 in the dev report.
- **The hosted wrapper the card cites was not read.** The card's evidence names a wrapper in the hosted product as prior art (a closed decision, the candidates, a finished sentence). That repository is not readable from this session, so its value names were not compared: NOT MEASURED. The four values here come from the card, the ruling record, D3 and the executor on `main` (`findDatasetTermCandidates`, the `listDatasets` fill).
- **The `Skills-docs:` line.** `skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md` is on `main`; it follows `nextStep` and cites `sourceLine` only once #34919 fills them, so the edit is owed after that card.
- **Plain `z.object`, as the sibling output schemas.** The strictness count for `ai/` moves 97 to 98 object sites; `ai/` is an untriaged directory in that ledger.
- **Body layout.** The two HTML comments (first and last line) and the footer are the dispatching seat's ordered layout for the relay.
- **Shallow clone.** This checkout is shallow. No claim here rests on history dates or ancestry.
